title: Customers with High-Value Orders
description:
Return the names and emails of customers who have placed **at least one order worth more than 250**. Use `IN` with a subquery.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`, `city`, `country`

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`

Output columns: `name`, `email`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com','New York','USA'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com','London','UK'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com','Chicago','USA'),(4,'Dan','dan@example.com','Mumbai','India'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-05','completed',100.00),(2,2,DATE '2026-01-06','completed',300.00),(3,3,DATE '2026-01-07','completed',150.00),(4,4,DATE '2026-01-08','completed',500.00),(5,1,DATE '2026-01-09','completed',280.00);
solution_sql: SELECT name, email FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders WHERE total_amount > 250) ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: Alice (order 280), Bob (order 300), Dan (order 500) qualify; Carol's max is 150

hints: The subquery returns customer_ids with at least one qualifying order.
IN (subquery) tests whether the outer column matches any value in the subquery result.
explanation: `IN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders WHERE total_amount > 250)` collects ids 1 (Alice, order 280), 2 (Bob, 300), 4 (Dan, 500). Customer 3 (Carol, max 150) is not in the set.
